core_obligations: Use quasi-compactness of the U_i and the cited refinement lemma to choose finite subsets K'_i of the covering index sets K_i (proof lines 5584-5586).
Use surjectivity of the resulting map to find coverings of each V_j and a commutative diagram refining the presentation into finite products over K'_i (proof lines 5587-5605).
Use quasi-compactness of the V_j and the same refinement lemma to choose finite subsets M'_j of the new index sets (proof lines 5606-5609).

Define the finite index set L as the disjoint union of the products K'_i x K'_i and of the M'_j, set W_l to be the fibre product U_{ik} x_{U_i} U_{ik'} for the product indices and V_{jm} for the others, and conclude that the resulting diagram has the required properties up to line 5624 (proof lines 5610-5624).
proof_roadmap: Cut the given coverings down to finite subfamilies using quasi-compactness.
Refine the presentation by coverings of the second family of objects.
Cut again and build the index set from products and the new finite sets.
difficulty_reason: The lemma refines a given presentation by direct images of the structure sheaf along members of a basis into a presentation whose first terms are indexed by a finite set of intersections and coverings from the basis, in such a way that the horizontal maps induce an isomorphism on cokernels. The proof first uses quasi-compactness of the U_i to choose finite subfamilies of the given coverings, then uses surjectivity of the resulting map to find coverings of the V_j and a commutative diagram refining the presentation, and finally uses quasi-compactness of the V_j again to cut those coverings down to finite subfamilies, defining the index set L as a disjoint union of products of the finite index sets and of the V-indexed finite sets and choosing the corresponding basis members as intersections (proof lines 5583-5624). H2: the two successive applications of the quasi-compact refinement and the construction of the index set L with the intersections are the substance.
